bus.via: Budva, Autobuska Stanica to Kotor, Autobuska Stanica

trips.route_note: Take a direct bus from Budva bus station to Kotor bus station, about 1 hour, with frequent departures; the old town is a short walk from the bus station.
trips.why: The direct bus takes about 35 minutes, departs frequently, and drops you a short walk from the old town.
know: Kotor's old town is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The bus station is a short walk from the old town, so you don't need a taxi at either end.
Wear sturdy shoes, since the old town streets and the climb to the fortress walls are steep.

trips.route_note: Take a bus from Budva to Kotor bus station, then a local bus or taxi along the bay to Perast, about 30 minutes; allow extra time for return connections.
see: Church of Our Lady of the Rocks
trips.tour_query: Perast and Kotor day trip from Budva
trips.why: The trip is about 51 minutes by road, and the bus route needs a change at Kotor with uncertain connections, so a taxi (about 30 USD) is the simpler choice.
know: Allow extra time for the return connections if you go by bus.
Perast is small and walkable, so a few hours is usually enough.
Boats to Our Lady of the Rocks run from Perast.

bus.via: Budva, Autobuska Stanica to Cetinje, Autobuska Stanica

trips.route_note: Take a direct bus from Budva to Cetinje bus station, about 1 hour via the mountain road; buses run regularly and the centre is walkable from the station.
trips.why: The direct bus takes about 37 minutes over the mountain road and drops you in the walkable centre.
know: Cetinje was the historic royal capital of Montenegro, with several museums and historic buildings in the centre.
The centre is walkable from the bus station, so the bus alone covers the trip.
The route climbs into the mountains, so expect winding roads and some motion sickness risk on the bus.
